text:
Our World: The week of Nov. 23, 2026
Monitor staffers and contributors share their challenges and insights from reporting around the globe.
Russia makes offshore nuclear pitch to Africa
The Kremlin wants to bring floating nuclear power plants to Africa, Russian leader Vladimir Putin told delegates at a recent Russia-Africa summit in Moscow. Floating power plants are already big business in Africa, with the Turkish company Karpowership providing diesel-generated electricity from offshore plants in eight countries. They are a popular alternative to conventional plants because they can be set up more quickly. However, potential pitfalls include the dependence they create on foreign entities for basic services like keeping lights on.  
– Ryan Lenora Brown
China seeks protections for gig economy workers
China’s labor ministry has released draft rules to set nationwide protections for gig economy workers – a rapidly expanding segment of the country’s workforce. The rules establish standards for working hours, rest periods, minimum pay, and collective bargaining for gig workers such as food delivery drivers. They also increase employers’ responsibility for the workers, in part, by limiting the use of automatic algorithms to penalize employees. China has some 320 million people – or 44% of the workforce – in “flexible employment,” meaning they have no full-time contract, up from 280 million last year, according to the Chinese publication Sixth Tone.  – Ann Scott Tyson
“Tulum is a magnet”
That’s Tito Juárez, who provides water-based services to tourists, speaking to the newspaper El País about the resort town on Mexico’s Caribbean coast. Tulum is famous for its archaeological sites, pristine beaches, and turquoise waters. Despite these attractions, the tourism business there is hurting. International airlines have cut back on flights to the area. Visits from abroad are down more than 40% this year, according to the Financial Times. A big reason? Sargassum. The foul-smelling seaweed is covering the beaches of Tulum and other locations on the coast. Mexican officials are promoting a campaign called Tulum Renace (Tulum Reborn) to clean up the beaches and help revive tourism.  – Matthew Bell    
“A hugely significant milestone”
That’s how conservationist Cat Barlow described the fledging of a golden eagle chick from a nest on a grouse moor in southern Scotland. The area’s birds of prey have been illegally targeted in the past to protect red grouse populations for sport shooting. The new chick, named Beaky Junior, is one of four descended from birds brought to the area after the population’s decline, according to ITV News. Support from landowners and gamekeepers has helped the numbers in southern Scotland rise to more than 50, the highest for three centuries.  – Tim Backshall
